proof_checks.common_grade_work_formula: The formula D(A,B) = sum_{v in A \triangle B} c_v(g)^2 is correctly derived. The v16.23 O1/O3 rules ensure that a retained subtree keeps its subtotal, so c_v(E_A g) = 1_{v in A} c_v(g). The v15.40 work pairing sums the squared differences of these subtotals over all edges, yielding the stated formula.
proof_checks.separation_and_zero_subtotals: Coordinates with zero weight c_v(g)^2 do not contribute to the work. If two views have the same effective mask on the remaining coordinates, their distance is zero, which violates the separation axiom of the metric test.
proof_checks.meet_and_join_closure_proof: The proof is valid. In a meet-closed catalog, any nearest pair must be comparable by inclusion; otherwise, their intersection would be in the catalog and strictly closer to both, contradicting the minimum distance m. For join-closed catalogs, complementing the masks reduces the problem to the meet-closed case.
proof_checks.neighbor_pair_ties_computation: At the lower endpoint A of a minimum edge A \subsetneq B, any other neighbor C must have disjoint additions/removals from B relative to A (otherwise their intersection/union would provide a closer view). Thus D(B,C) = 2m for all three other neighbors C. This results in three maximizing pairs containing B, which violates the opposite gate's requirement of exactly two disjoint maximizing pairs.
proof_checks.v15_42_gates_inspection: The v15.42 operational complex construction strictly requires every vertex to have exactly four neighbors (degree gate) and exactly two disjoint maximizing pairs among the six pairs of neighbors (opposite gate). The proof correctly identifies that closure forces a violation of these gates.
proof_checks.argument_dependencies: The argument relies purely on the algebraic properties of the views and the v15.42 geometric gates. It does not require all neighbors across the catalog, a physical receiver, or any v15.43 input schema.
proof_checks.fixture_catalogs_reconstruction: The four catalogs are correctly reconstructed. The 25-square catalog has minimum distance 4 and 50 edges. The 35-view catalog adds 10 isolated strips (degree 0). The 26-view catalog adds one shared side, dropping the minimum distance to 2 and leaving 23 squares isolated. The 101-view closure has minimum distance 1, with 125 edges and degrees 25 (empty), 5 (singletons), 2 (sides), and 0 (squares).
proof_checks.source_preparation_critique: The operational complex requires a carefully restricted catalog (only the squares). The presence of intermediate strips or their intersections breaks the geometry. The argument correctly identifies that an inherited operational reason is needed to explain why an owner would only compare the square views and exclude the others.
